thread:
sam: quick heads-up — I ran a side-by-side perf loop across clouds for the 7B quantized candidate (int8) and saw a weird p99 skew on GCP compared to AWS/Azure. attaching quick numbers and a couple logs. :eyes:

sam: runs: AWS g5.12x (driver 535.xx / CUDA 12.1) | GCP a2-highgpu-1g (driver 530.xx / CUDA 11.8) | Azure ND A10v5 (driver 535.xx / CUDA 12.1)

sam: micro-bench harness: 1k requests, batch=1, seq=512, model=redwood-7b-q8, tok gen only, 4 threads pmux

perf-bot: summary (median / p99 latency):
- aws: 48ms / 118ms
- gcp: 61ms / 185ms  <-- big tail
- azure: 51ms / 125ms

marta: :thinking: interesting. same batch/seq and same quantized model? did the build use the same libtorch/cuBLAS combo on GCP image?

sam: yes same docker image SHA, we pin wheel + libtorch, but the base AMI on GCP uses driver 530 and system CUDA 11.8. container sees 12.1 libs but kernel-driver mismatch possible.

liam: driver vs userland mismatch can force fallback kernels (cublas/cudnn selecting safe algos). also NCCL/env differences can influence scheduler fairness and I/O on multi-tenant hosts.

marta: can you paste the repro command and the relevant envs you used?

sam: yep — command we ran:
```
docker run --gpus all --rm \
  -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
  -e CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 \
  -e CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=LAZY \
  -v /mnt/model:/models/model:ro \
  redwood/infer:prod-2026-03 \
  python /app/bench/throughput.py --model /models/model --seq 512 --batch 1 --iters 1000
```

marta: two quick checks:
- try `export CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:16:8` vs disabled to see if algorithm nondeterminism is changing picks.
- run a small GEMM microbenchmark (cutlass or torch.matmul) at the same sizes under `nsys` to capture selected kernels.

alex: also compare cuBLAS versions inside the container on each host: `strings /usr/local/lib/libcublas.so | grep CUBLAS` and check `ldd` used libs. small mismatch (e.g. app linking to cublasLt v11) can change GEMM path.

sam: did a quick `ldd` check earlier — GCP node resolved to /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (system) vs container's /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcublas.so

liam: that could explain it. system driver older -> driver shim yields extra syncs -> tail latency.

marta: also note that quantized kernels sometimes fall back to reference GEMM kernels on certain driver+cuBLAS combos. that would blow up p99 even if median ok.

perf-bot: profile snippet (nsys sample) from a single slow GCP request:
```
Time   Kernel                  Duration
0.102s cublasGemmEx            79.4ms
0.185s fallback_gemm_ref       84.1ms
0.269s memcpy H2D              12ms
```

sam: that fallback_gemm_ref entry is the smoking gun. It shows both cublasGemmEx and a later reference kernel. AWS/Azure runs show contiguous cublasLt fast-kernels.

alex: try forcing cublasLt path explicitly in PyTorch (if available) or upgrade the system driver on GCP nodes to the 535 line. Also test `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG` off to avoid determinism overhead.

marta: quick experiment idea — run the same bench with CUDA 11.8 userlibs vs 12.1 userlibs on GCP but with driver 535 (if you can upgrade) and see if p99 aligns.

sam: scheduling a micro-run on a GCP node with driver 535 now. will also run int8 vs fp16 to see if kernel selection differs by dtype. ETA ~30m.

liam: keep an eye on firmware too (GPU BIOS). had one case where A100 firmware mismatch changed TPC scheduling and pushed p99s up.

sam: results update: after bumping GCP driver to 535.xx and re-running same container image:
- gcp (drv 535/CUDA 12.1): 50ms / 128ms
- still slightly worse than AWS but much better than 185ms p99. int8 -> still shows occasional fallback at 1/5000 requests.

marta: residual fallback could be due to kernel selector heuristics hitting a bad-case for seq=512 + batch=1. try slightly increasing batch to 2 and see if selector picks a different algo.

sam: batch=2 on GCP (drv535): 78ms / 140ms (median up as expected, p99 improved modestly). makes sense.

alex: can we add a tiny synthetic that pins the workload distribution (prefix caching enabled vs disabled) — caching can hide fallback pressure.

sam: added note to the CI job: run nightly microbench across clouds, check for fallback_gemm_ref in profiles, alert if p99 increases >25% vs baseline. opened infra ticket #INF-3242 to coord driver upgrades and a nightly job.

marta: awesome. also add a check for `libcublas` soname mismatch in the job and graph p50/p90/p99 by driver+cuda.

sam: will add logs and upload perf traces to the bench bucket. thanks all :pray:
